decisive_join: Join institution-authored success labels, historically selected survivors, unobserved rejects, deployment feedback, and shared-vendor reuse without treating correlation as causal proof of merit.

findings.claim: Learning from selected survivors is selection-conditioned learning, not neutral observation of the full applicant population.
limits: The size and direction of bias require deployment-specific data.

findings.claim: Institutional resemblance can be reported as prediction when labels encode prior selection, opportunity allocation, ratings, and sponsorship.
limits: A real correlation may exist even when the causal interpretation is weak.

findings.claim: Shared-vendor screening creates a plausible cross-employer monoculture risk rather than guaranteeing independent market correction.
limits: Vendor architecture, employer configuration, human overrides, and study scope remain to be recovered.

selection_rule: Every model claim must expose the target, selected sample, opportunity allocation, missing labels, exploration policy, and cross-employer reuse before prediction can be interpreted.

prohibited_inferences: correlation among incumbents establishes causal job merit
removing protected attributes removes proxy effects
using one vendor means every employer makes an identical decision

title: Selection-conditioned learning: the institution predicts resemblance to its survivors
